newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria names panel on political detainees.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria names panel on political detainees.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has named a panel to look into the cases of political detainees held without trial under a measure known as Decree Two.

The official gazette, published in the capital Abuja on Thursday, said the attorney-general and national security adviser would sit on the panel headed by the inspector-general of police, to make recommendations on all those held under the decree.
"If the Head of State accepts the recommendation, he shall direct that the order be revoked and cause the inspector-general of police to release the person immediately," the gazette said.
Dozens of people are detained under the decree, including human rights lawyer Gani Fawehinmi.
But Nigeria's most prominent detainees, presidential contender Moshood Abiola and former president Olusegun Obasanjo, are not held under Decree Two.

Abiola faces a treason trial for declaring himself president in 1994 based on results from a 1993 election annulled by a previous military government, plunging Africa's most populous nation into crisis.
Obasanjo is serving a 15-year sentence for his part in an alleged coup plot.
Nigeria has come under fire from Western countries for human rights abuses and lack of democracy.

A group of ministers from the Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies is to meet in New York at the weekend to decide whether to impose sanctions on Nigeria, suspended after the execution of nine minority rights activists in November.

The London-based group Human Rights Watch/Africa in a 52-page report released on Friday called on the Commonwealth ministers to impose sanctions on Nigeria, saying the Abuja government was violating its citizens' rights with impunity.
Abuja said it would begin reviewing the cases of those held under the Decree Two in June, after the report of a United Nations fact-finding mission.
